text: Hello to all of our viewers. Dear
viewers, this afternoon we are
witnessing three very important
developments. The first development is
President Trump's welcome ceremony for
Mr. Xi Jinping. Mr. Xi and his wife,
Peng Liyuan, have officially landed at
Joint Base Andrews. And President Trump
, along with the First Lady, arrived to
welcome them. We have a number of
related developments as well. The
second development concerns the civil
war in Iran. It seems Iran is at risk
of losing its first province, a
province located furthest to the
southeast: Sistan and Baluchestan. We
all know that an Iranian general has
been killed there. In addition, a
high-ranking officer from Iran's
intelligence sector has also been
killed. Therefore, the conflict here
has reached an alarming level, and Iran
is at risk of losing this region. For
the third development, we have some
statements from a Russian official. We
previously thought that Ukrainians
understood Russia best, but in reality,
it must be said that Russians
understand Russians best. They have
pointed out a fundamental reason why
Russia is losing so miserably and is at
risk of such a collapse. I invite you
all to join us for the detailed content
. First, this is the image of President
Trump welcoming Mr. Xi; it was not the
B-2 Spirit, but the B-1B Lancer. You
can see the image of the B-1B rushing
by; it flew low, so the sound it
produced was very loud. President Trump
was very expressive, but you can see
that Mr. Xi Jinping's face remained
expressionless. There are some
observations that Mr. Xi's health is
not good. Although it is not too bad,
there are some signs suggesting that
his complexion is not good. In
particular, there is a detail that
people have pointed out: when walking
down the stairs, Mr. Xi's hand had to
grip tightly onto the hand of his wife,
Ms. Peng. This is because, although
walking down stairs seems simple, many
heads of state have stumbled. Even
President Trump has slipped once, and
Mr. Biden has tripped many times.
Therefore, as he walked down, Mr. Xi
had to grip his wife's hand tightly. It
is precisely because of such a grand
welcome that left-wing media outlets
are complaining that President Trump is
too favorable toward Mr. Xi and the
reception is too formal. However, we
must look at the results, because while
Presidents Obama and Biden were tough
on Mr. Xi, Fox News analyzed that they
subsequently handed over valuable
American factories to China. The entire
production chain shifted completely to
China during the Obama and Biden eras.
But what about President Trump? First,
he had to reverse all of those
disastrous policies. Second, he
launched a trade war. Third, he cut off
China's proxy forces and severed
China's influence in the international
arena, such as in Venezuela, Cuba, or
Iran. As of now, President Trump has
completed the reception program and has
returned to the White House. But in an
interview, President Trump mentioned
that all the tech leaders, such as Elon
Musk, the billionaires from Google,
ChatGPT, Facebook, Amazon, Bruzone, and
others, will all be attending the
evening banquet. In addition,
billionaires in the financial industry
will also attend, and Elon Musk will
also be there. The White House has
officially announced the agenda, which
starts from 8:00 AM tomorrow until 8:00
PM tomorrow. This is the official day
of reception. After that, on the 25th,
Mr. Xi will return home. We have this
first official welcoming ceremony at
10:00. Following that is a series of
private meetings and press interviews.
Then the two sides will hold private
talks. And then, it will be time for
the evening banquet. Starting at 6:45,
President Trump will welcome Mr. Xi and
First Lady Peng. The bilateral meeting
will take place at 11:30, where both
sides will discuss issues such as the
trade war, AI, or hot topics around the
world. After that, at 12:00, another
meeting will continue. In general,
these meetings last quite a long time.
We turn to some developments regarding
the Iran hot spot. This is the
government military force of the
Islamic Republic deployed to carry out
a rescue. Because after the two latest
clashes, Iran's government forces are
losing ground. Even one of their
brigadier generals was killed, and a
senior officer of the intelligence
force was also eliminated. Therefore,
you can see many pickup trucks carrying
military forces and weapons arriving in
the Sistan and Baluchestan region. It
seems that as we are speaking here, a
second round of fighting is taking
place and Iran's government troops
continue to send reinforcements.
Open-source intelligence organizations
assess that the latest fighting in the
Sistan and Baluchestan province is very
serious. Actually, the scale is not yet
large, but in the context where the
Islamic Republic of Iran is weak and
exhausted, it has suffered heavy losses
right in the first battles. This
morning, I reported to you that the
death of Brigadier General Hossein Jifi
has been confirmed, and the funeral
will be held tomorrow, Friday.
Additionally, there is a senior
intelligence officer, he is Ahmad
Nrezati. He seems to be a major or a
lieutenant colonel, and it has also
been confirmed that he was killed. The
assessment from the open-source
intelligence group Dec Conflict is like
decoding the wars. They say that Iran
is facing a great deal of instability.
Firstly, its internal situation is
unstable, its economy is unstable,
there is great pressure from the
outside, and pressure from the inside
is also great. And we should closely
monitor the hostilities in Sistan and
Baluchestan province. Because if the
fighting breaks out at a high intensity
rather than being intermittent—
actually, its intensity is now daily,
already considered high intensity—
then this could be the straw that
breaks the camel's back, it could be
the place where the domino effect of
collapse begins. Imagine if Iran sends
too many forces to the far southeast,
they will leave their northwestern
flank exposed, right? In that area,
there are many Kurds. Therefore, it can
be said that Iran is being pushed into
a very difficult situation. We move on
to the third development. A senior
Russian official decodes the reasons
why they failed and why Russia cannot
develop. Now, Russian leaders
themselves must admit that the Russian
Federation is throwing away its own
future. An ineffective bureaucratic
apparatus is pushing the country toward
irreparable stagnation. I emphasize
that this is not a journalist, not a
citizen, and not a military blogger,
but a Russian nationalist leader.
Dmitry Demushkin. This is his full
statement. There is less and less
freedom. But the problem does not lie
in freedom or in our personal feelings
about it. Many people think, "Oh, less
freedom is fine, I don't need it, I'll
just live my life." But the real
problem is that the state apparatus is
operating ineffectively. Furthermore,
the problem is that many people do not
understand that we are throwing away
our own future, a future for decades to
come. And sadly, we don't dislike this
model because we can't integrate into
it. That is not the case at all.
Personally, I might have enough of my
own social projects to assert myself in
some capacity. The issue is that we
will lag behind irreparably and become
weak. This lag will continue to grow
and become increasingly severe. Unlike
bad democracies, even very bad ones.
They still have mechanisms for renewal,
the replacement of leadership teams,
and competition, so in the end, they
survive. Conversely, even the strongest
and most efficient dictatorship, sadly,
often collapses, taking the whole
system and the country down with it.
That is truly a tragedy. I am not
saying that this country will
definitely collapse—heaven forbid. I
do not claim that, nor do I wish for it
to happen. I only want to emphasize
that inefficiency is the core problem,
not the opposition at all. In a
dictatorship, there is no such thing as
an opposition. Just look at any such
system; it is never changed in a
democratic way. No dictatorship has
ever been overthrown or collapsed based
on legal grounds, nor has any dissident
ever brought one down. Such regimes
collapse from within themselves. That
is the real issue, and it has nothing
to do with members of the opposition.
One could find a way to ensure that
Russia has absolutely no opposition
figures left at all. But sadly. That
does not mean we will live happily and
the country will prosper. If the
problem were simply that, perhaps
ignoring those opposition members
wouldn't matter. Furthermore, there are
currently two rumors in Russia that the
Russian media loves to repeat. The
first is that Russia attacked Ukraine
to retaliate against Ukrainian attacks.
And the second is that Russia is not
using its full arsenal against Ukraine
for humanitarian reasons. However, the
Russian nationalist leader Dmitry
Demushkin has refuted both of these
rumors. He said almost every type of
weapon has already been used against
Ukraine. Perhaps excluding only nuclear
, biological, and chemical weapons, all
other weapons have been deployed. They
have even attacked with non-nuclear
versions of intercontinental Oreshnik
missiles. Therefore, whether it be
Iskander, Dagger, Kalibr, or any other
type, they have all been used. So where
else is there room for escalation?
Every weapon is sent straight to the
battlefield and put into use
immediately upon production. Very few
people pay attention to the elections
in Russia. Because their results are
clear to me, to you, and to the people
there. However, I see once again a
tremendous passivity among the people
toward political issues. Because many
have concluded that they themselves
cannot decide anything and that
elections lead to no results, so they
simply don't bother to vote anymore.
Thus, we are seeing Russian citizens
from all social classes—from
commoners and officials to
intellectuals—all feeling very
pessimistic about the future of the
country. Below, I would like to share
with you another perspective from the
intellectual community. He is a lawyer
and a well-known Russian analyst named
Ivan Mironov. He says that the hearts
of us Russians have become completely
calloused and cold. Violence has become
deeply ingrained in our people. All
limits, policies, and ideologies
socially acceptable to be opened have
already been flung wide open. Truly,
almost all of them. Every time we think
we have hit rock bottom, there is a
knock from below. There still exists a
deep, gaping abyss. But that is perhaps
hell itself. Perhaps we are already
lying right inside that very hell.
Almost all neighboring countries are
also looking at us with suspicion. It
seems everything will end the way the
Finns did it. That is, they built a
fence of blades along their border.
Clearly, we are moving further and
further away from common sense, and we
have forgotten what common sense really
is. Moreover, common sense now has
become the most disgusting form of
madness. Sometimes honest, fair, and
sincere people look around and feel as
if they might be the ones who have gone
mad, that everything must exist exactly
the way it is laid out before them. And
black turns out to be white, while
white is, in reality, black. Clearly, a
picture of Russian society couldn't be
more pessimistic, coming from two
representatives: officials and
intellectuals; they both see it, and
especially they know that authoritarian
regimes all share such a common end.
They see absolutely no other path, only
the paths that the likes of Bashar
al-Assad, Iran, or Maduro are currently
on. Next, Danny will bring you
President Trump's speech at the United
Nations. Because this speech is
relatively long, Danny will focus on
three main topics. One is the conflict
in Iran. Two is the International
Criminal Court (ICC), which President
Trump is calling on the whole world to
boycott. And the third topic is
artificial intelligence; there is a
global battle over how to use AI,
whether to regulate it or to continue
its explosive development. Here are
those three points from President Trump
. First is the issue of the war in Iran
. President Trump said, "As president
of the most extraordinary nation in
history, I have no intention of letting
dangers grow for one more day." I do
not believe in letting problems fester;
they only become harder to solve. So,
while others talked, I took action.
While others spoke about peace, I
created peace. While others ignored
threats, I confronted them. While
others spoke of courage, the United
States demonstrated that courage. While
others promised strength, I used that
strength to make the United States the
most powerful nation in the world.
Working with many nations in this room,
we are tackling challenges that have
existed for decades, we are finishing
work that has been left undone for
years, and we are doing very well.
There is no clearer example of a danger
allowed to gather strength and threaten
the world than the world’s leading
state sponsor of terror. That is the
Islamic Republic of Iran. For 51 years,
the fanatical Iranian regime has ruled
through bloodshed and mass murder,
spreading death, slaughter, and chaos
throughout the Middle East and beyond.
They were once the bully of the Middle
East, but they are no longer the bully.
From the very first day I entered
politics, my stance has never wavered.
I will never allow Iran to have nuclear
weapons. After taking office in 2025, I
immediately opened negotiations with
Iran and offered comprehensive economic
cooperation in exchange for them ending
their nuclear program and stopping
their support for terror. But they
refused. They refused completely, and
that was a big mistake. Then, in the
midnight Sledgehammer operation, the
United States military destroyed their
nuclear program, burying it under
mountains of rubble. And once again, I
urged Iran to reach an agreement, and
once again, they refused. The regime
continues to build a massive arsenal of
missiles and drones. At the same time,
it threatens the security of every U.S.
service member in the region, as well
as everyone else there. They are also
building a type of missile capable of
reaching Europe, and they are very
proud of it. I hope Europeans realize
that Iran’s goal is to finish its mad
race to build an atomic bomb under the
cover of this conventional ballistic
missile shield. But if they succeed,
that evil regime will be free to spread
terror and death forever. Knowing that
any effort to stop them will be met
with an arsenal capable of atomic
destruction. The Iranian regime itself
has murdered more than 72,000 of its
own citizens this year. Recently,
10,000 people were killed for
protesting. Imagine if such a vile
regime gained the ability to carry out
large-scale terrorist attacks under the
cover of a nuclear shield. That is the
reality we must face, a reality that
too many have chosen to ignore. They
all looked away; many presidents and
many others just wanted to look away.
They did not want to do anything about
the problem, even though they knew it
existed. After giving Iran every
opportunity to reach an agreement, I
acted to ensure that neither the United
States nor any other nation would ever
have to face such a nightmare, such a
catastrophic problem. The result of
Operation Epic Fury is that all 159
warships of the Iranian navy are now
lying at the bottom of the sea. All
other military capabilities of Iran
have also been dismantled. But moving
forward, will a deal be reached with
Iran, a deal that allows them to
rebuild and construct a nation far
greater than it has ever been, one that
could become one of the greatest
nations in the Middle East or even the
world? Or will I destroy the Islamic
Republic of Iran and do it very quickly
, never giving them another chance to
kill, nor a chance to destroy people
and other nations ever again? Will I
send them to hell, with no chance of
survival and no hope for a great future
or for future generations? But I
believe we will reach a deal right
after the election. They are waiting to
see how I fare in the midterms. What
they don’t realize is that I’m not
running. I already did that in 2024 and
I won in a landslide. We won with a
massive, overwhelming victory and I
will be here for another two and a half
years. I do not consider the election a
factor at all, nor will I consider it a
factor when it comes to the issue of
Iran. It doesn’t even cross my mind.
The only thing I think about is that
Iran will never have nuclear weapons.
Cowards and traitors. Cowards and
traitors love to say that the United
States is running out of ammunition,
but that is not true. We have more
ammunition than we could ever even
think about using. And we are producing
them at a level never seen before. We
are replenishing our stockpiles faster
than at any time in the past. And
it’s all the most state-of-the-art
equipment. Also, in the very near
future, our massive ammunition plants
will start operations. There are
currently 18 such plants being built by
the largest defense companies in the
world. 18 plants are under construction
. Some will be finished very quickly.
They are almost done. And that rapid
pace of construction will lead to very
fast deployment of all types of
missiles and all types of ammunition,
and we will be able to supply our
allies at a much faster rate than today
. I have called on all nations to join
us in enforcing complete economic
isolation on Iran until they stop their
attacks on commercial vessels, abandon
their nuclear ambitions, and cease
their support for terrorist
organizations. This Iranian terrorist
regime is behaving very badly. Not
because they are strong and confident,
but because they are weak and desperate
. If we stand together, we will soon
see a world free from the 51-year-long
Iranian terrorist threat, and oil
prices will drop sharply, even lower
than when the conflict began. And in
the United States, at that time, oil
prices will be very low; with courage
and determination, anything is possible
. The second topic President Trump
addressed is the International Criminal
Court, the ICC. Mr. Trump said the
following. The United States also
strongly opposes the out-of-control
organization known as the International
Criminal Court. We will never allow
U.S. service members or anyone else to
be investigated or put on show trials
by an anti-American court that has no
jurisdiction over us, or by a group of
bad actors. I call on all nations that
are members of the International
Criminal Court, the ICC, to formally
withdraw from this rogue organization
immediately. There is one more topic
that President Trump also addressed,
which is artificial intelligence, AI.
But now, President Trump does not call
it AI anymore, but calls it SI, which
stands for Super Intelligence.
President Trump stated the following.
The United States also completely
rejects any attempt to build a global
system to control artificial
intelligence. Which is being talked
about a lot right now. From now on, it
will officially be called super
intelligence. We will change the name.
Using the word "artificial" makes
intelligence sound fake. It makes
people feel like it is something fake,
but it is not fake. In fact, it is
quite amazing. We must be careful. In
reality, it is completely opposite to
what the name currently suggests. From
this moment on, all United States
documents and hopefully the whole world
will be changed to use a much more
accurate term, super intelligent, which
means super intelligence. In other
words, we will say welcome to the new
world of super intelligence. SI, no
longer AI. It sounds much better and is
much more accurate. Finally, President
Trump concluded if we move forward with
strength and unity to stand against the
enemies of all mankind. If we reject
the voices that want us to succumb to
fear and doubt, if we refuse to shrink
from our responsibilities to our people
, then together through bold actions.
We will make this world much safer and
much better. Thank you everyone. Dear
viewers, those were some great
discussions about the future of Russia
and the future of the world from a
high-ranking Russian official and
President Trump. What do you think
about these speeches? I invite you to
help Dani by leaving your opinions in
the comments section. Anny would like
to thank you and see you again in the
next program. Thank you very much.
